digest.component_or_area: overlap judge LLM call batching and prompt caching
propositions: Judging candidates one per call re-sends the 846-token system prefix 2N times for N candidates, wasting input tokens despite hoisting the query digest into the system block in story 8415.
Batching multiple candidates into a single call per ordering reduces judge calls from 2N to 2*ceil(N/batch), directly removing prefix copies and saving ~8,460 tokens on six-candidate corpora.
The batch protocol description in the system prompt grows the cacheable prefix past the 1024-token floor, enabling prompt caching to read-back previously written prefix tokens across calls.

Judging multiple candidates side-by-side introduces cross-contamination risk where shared artifacts or neighboring verdicts bleed between candidates, requiring empirical precision measurement against per-pair baseline.

Real API measurement on identical six-candidate corpus shows batching reduces input tokens from 18,494 (8415) to 9,116 (−50.7%), enables cache_write 1,331 and cache_read 1,331 tokens, but shifts relation labels on 6/12 ordered pairs toward conservative verdicts.
